titleEn: You Can Cry. Wipe on My Apron!

pages.text: "All the olives picked!" Lulu ran across the yard holding a basket. Three cousins chased behind. Autumn sunshine had dried the yard soil hard.
A stone caught Lulu's foot. Crash! A stinging knee! The basket tipped, olives rolling away. Lulu's eyes burned, nose tingling.

Three cousins stopped a few steps ahead and looked down. Lulu raised both shoulders, pressed lips shut, and squeezed both eyes closed. "No crying. I am grown." But holding in made the throat sore and chest tight.
Mom hurried from the kitchen and bent to meet Lulu's eyes. "That hurt, did it not? You have been holding back tears."
"Your knee hurts, and losing the olives is upsetting?" Lulu nodded, eyelids swollen. "Crying helps. You may cry in front of your cousins too."
Mom opened both arms and shook out her apron. "Come. Have a good cry here." Lulu buried a face in it and cried freely.
After a long cry, the tight chest relaxed. Lulu wiped the tears on the apron and looked up. A round wet mark stayed behind. "You can cry. Wipe on my apron!"
Three cousins gathered the olives and brought the basket. "All here, Lulu!" Lulu reached both forepaws out with a big smile. The bell jingled.
Days later, something upsetting happened again. Lulu did not hold it in. At the kitchen threshold, Lulu said, "Mom, I am sad. One, say you are sad! Two, do not hold it in! Three, run to the apron!"
Mom hugged Lulu in her apron. After a good cry, only a mark remained there, and Lulu's heart felt light. You can cry. Wipe on my apron! "Shall we pick olives now?" She wiped Lulu's cheek.
